big_questions.question: Identity — Who am I, really?
big_questions.why_central: The plot is built to peel one name off a man and press another onto him. Smith confronts Neo with his split existence and offers to erase the 'Anderson' record in exchange for Morpheus (ev-007); a disembodied voice then names him 'the One' and demands a single 'Yes' before he has any reason to believe it (ev-008). He actively rejects the title — 'denies being the One' (ev-032) — yet acts as the One, so the story holds the label suspended between destiny and decision until he finally claims it on

evidence.grounding: Smith lays out Neo's two lives and offers to wipe his record clean in return for Morpheus.
A voice calls him 'the One' and requires a single 'Yes' before he has grounds to accept it.
Neo denies being the One, so his rescue is a wager on a man rather than a prophecy.
Only after death and revival does he seize the identity, halting bullets and reading the room as code.

big_questions.question: Truth vs. a comfortable lie — Is it better to know an unbearable reality or to live a pleasant illusion?
big_questions.why_central: This is the story's literal switch. Morpheus reframes Neo's lifelong dread as an enslaving system and offers him two exits — forget or know — and Neo swallows the red pill (ev-010). The honest answer costs him: he recoils as the world is revealed to be a simulation and humans farmed for power, an 'unbearable violation' (ev-013). Cypher is the counter-argument made flesh, tasting an 'impossible steak' and bargaining to be re-plugged into the lie (ev-020).

evidence.grounding: Morpheus recasts Neo's dread as an enslaving system and offers a choice between forgetting and knowing; Neo takes the red pill.
Neo recoils as he learns the world is a simulation and humans are farmed — the truth is an unbearable violation.
Cypher savors a fabricated steak and bargains to be returned to ignorant comfort.

big_questions.question: Meaning vs. pleasure — A life of purposeful suffering or empty satisfaction?
big_questions.why_central: Cypher's arc states this question most purely. He recasts Morpheus's prophecy as 'a body count' (ev-020) and trades a hard, meaningful freedom for a soft, meaningless comfort. Neo travels the opposite route — from the hollow routine of Meta CorTechs (ev-005) toward a cause worth dying for (ev-032).

evidence.grounding: Neo's ordinary life is a mundane morning and an ultimatum about lateness and authority.
Cypher measures the cause only in deaths and chooses pleasure over purpose.
Neo commits to a dangerous rescue with no guarantee, choosing meaning over safety.

big_questions.question: Freedom vs. determinism (fate) — Do we choose, or is the path already written?
big_questions.why_central: The prophecy of the One and the Oracle's verdict (ev-014, ev-023) set up a world that seems pre-scripted, yet the characters keep acting against the script. Neo's refusal of the name and fate Smith 'pronounces' at the point of death (ev-039) is the story's loudest claim that choice overrides destiny.

evidence.grounding: Morpheus reframes the rescue as destiny through the myth of the One and the Oracle's prophecy.
Neo carries a private verdict and a death-prophecy he is ordered to keep.
At the edge of death Neo refuses the name and fate Smith pronounces and summons a surge that breaks the predicted outcome.

big_questions.question: Mortality — What does it mean to die, and can death be refused?
big_questions.why_central: Death is shown as both final and reversible. Mouse and the crew die and stay dead (ev-023, ev-029), giving mortality its weight, while Neo is shot three times and confirmed 'gone' (ev-044) — then called back. The story treats death as the one boundary whose rules the awakened can contest (ev-045).

evidence.grounding: Mouse is cornered and killed; death is presented as real and permanent.
Neo is shot three times, the life monitors flatline, and the crew gives him up — then Trinity's kiss restarts his heart.
Revived, he halts bullets and destroys an Agent, having crossed death and returned.

central_dilemma.name: Self-preservation vs. self-sacrifice — flee to save your own life, or risk it to save another's.
central_dilemma.horn_a: Preserve oneself: accept that Morpheus is lost, escape while escape is still possible, and live to fight another day.
central_dilemma.horn_b: Sacrifice for another: go back into a world that will kill you to pull out a man you cannot save by any logic.
central_dilemma.why_genuine: Both horns cost something the story has priced in. Choosing self costs Morpheus his life and costs Neo his emerging self-respect and the crew's trust; choosing sacrifice costs Neo any claim to safety and, by his own admission, he is 'not the One,' so the gamble carries no prophetic guarantee — only faith. evidence.grounding: Morpheus pins an Agent and orders Trinity to get Neo out, choosing to give his own life so the others escape — the sacrifice precedent.
Neo stops Morpheus's plug from being pulled and commits to going back in, denying he is the One, so the mission is a wager on a man, not a prophecy.
Cypher embodies the self-preservation horn, bargaining to save himself by betraying Morpheus and the crew.

conflicts.name: The Agents vs. the freed crew (the systemic hunt)
parties: Trinity, Morpheus, Neo and the Nebuchadnezzar crew
conflicts.stakes: The Agents enforce the simulation and eliminate anyone unplugged or threatening it; the crew fights to stay free and to free others.
conflicts.how_it_develops: Opens with the Agents cornering and nearly capturing Trinity (ev-001), escalates through the rooftop chase (ev-003) and the office/interrogation seizure of Neo (ev-006, ev-007), and culminates in the helicopter rescue and Neo's destruction of Smith (ev-034, ev-045).

evidence.grounding: Four cops breach Room 303 and take Trinity at gunpoint; Agent Smith reveals the raid's true cost, and Trinity breaks the arrest and kills the squad.
Trinity runs for a separate phone while Agents Brown, Jones and Smith close in across the rooftops.
A ringing phone becomes a real office raid; Neo slips past the searching Agents to a ledge he cannot cross.
Smith interrogates Neo and offers to wipe his record in exchange for Morpheus; on refusal, Neo's mouth is sealed and a tap-creature is implanted.
Neo drops a helicopter onto the executive office and guns down Agents Jones, Brown and Smith to extract Morpheus.
Revived, Neo halts the Agents' volley, reads the room as code, and bursts out of Smith, destroying him so the surviving Agents feel fear.

conflicts.name: Cypher's betrayal of the crew
parties: Morpheus, Neo, Trinity, Apoc, Switch, Dozer, Tank
conflicts.stakes: A disillusioned crew member trades his comrades to the Agents for reinsertion into the Matrix, nearly destroying the ship from within.
conflicts.how_it_develops: Cypher's resentment curdles into a secret deal with Smith (ev-020), he sabotages the Oracle trip (ev-021), then murders Apoc and Switch, delivers Morpheus, and is only stopped by a surviving Tank (ev-029).

evidence.grounding: Cypher recasts Morpheus's prophecy as a body count to unsettle Neo, then crosses into the Matrix and strikes a bargain with Agent Smith over a steak.
Cypher covertly connects a phone and drops it in a garbage can, foreshadowing his treachery during the Oracle trip.
Cypher shoots Tank, answers Trinity with a false 'accident' story, murders Apoc and Switch, delivers Morpheus to the Agents, and is struck down by the surviving Tank.

conflicts.name: Neo vs. the truth of the Matrix (initiation)
parties: The reality revealed by Morpheus / the Matrix itself
conflicts.stakes: Whether Neo can accept the unbearable truth of the simulation and the cost of freedom, or recoil back into denial.
conflicts.how_it_develops: Neo is drawn toward the truth (ev-004), resists the office raid (ev-006), chooses the red pill (ev-010), physically rejects the 'Desert of the Real' (ev-013), and only later commits to a personal wager to save Morpheus (ev-032).

evidence.grounding: Neo is contacted through his own machine and, against his plans, follows a white rabbit to meet Trinity, who approaches him by name.
Morpheus reframes Neo's lifelong dread as a real enslaving system and offers a choice between forgetting and knowing; Neo swallows the red pill.
Morpheus walks Neo through the truth of the Matrix; Neo resists every step and recoils from the crew as agents of an unbearable violation.
Neo stops the plug from being pulled on Morpheus and commits to rescuing him alive, denying he is the One and making the mission a wager on a man.

conflicts.name: Neo vs. Agent Smith (the destined duel)
conflicts.stakes: The personal, escalating confrontation between the prophesied One and the system's most committed enforcer.
conflicts.how_it_develops: Smith leads Neo's seizure and interrogation (ev-006, ev-007), hunts him through the subway where Neo first summons his power (ev-037, ev-039), and finally faces a transformed Neo who destroys him (ev-043, ev-045).

evidence.grounding: Smith's raid drives Neo to a window ledge he cannot cross, beginning their direct antagonism.
Smith negotiates for Morpheus, and on Neo's contemptuous refusal, seals his mouth and implants the tracker.
After their gunfight clicks empty, Neo and Smith trade blows until Smith chokes Neo by the third-rail; Neo refuses the fate Smith pronounces and hurls him into the tunnel ceiling.
Neo races toward door 303 under fire and is stopped cold by Agent Smith's point-blank shot.
Neo enters Agent Smith and bursts out of him, destroying the first Agent ever.

conflicts.name: The crew vs. the Sentinels (real-world survival)
parties: The Nebuchadnezzar crew (Morpheus, Trinity, Neo, Tank, Dozer)
conflicts.stakes: Physical survival of the ship and crew in the real world, running parallel to and colliding with the Matrix conflict.
conflicts.how_it_develops: A Sentinel forces the ship to hide and arm its EMP (ev-019); later the Sentinels breach the hull as Neo dies, driving Morpheus toward the EMP in despair (ev-044), and overrun the deck at the moment of Neo's awakening and escape (ev-046).

evidence.grounding: A Sentinel sweeping the sewer main forces the Nebuchadnezzar into a too-small supply line; the crew goes cold and silent while the machine glides over them.
As Neo flatlines in the Matrix, sentinels breach the hull in the real world while Morpheus reaches for the EMP in weeping despair.
Sentinels overrun the ship's main deck, descending on Morpheus at the EMP switch as Neo dives for the phone at Trinity's 'Now!'.

torn_between: The safety and routine of his known life as Thomas Anderson (the office, the paycheck, 'two grand' deals)
The dangerous, unverifiable pull toward the truth represented by Trinity and the white rabbit
internal_conflicts.what_it_costs: His entire former identity is destroyed: he is captured, his mouth is sealed shut, a tracking bug is implanted in his body, and he is physically ejected from the pod that sustained him, nearly drowning before being recovered.

evidence.grounding: Neo is told to follow a white rabbit; spotting the pin on Dujour's jacket, he goes out 'against his plan to work the next day.'
The night's pull collapses into a mundane morning; Neo curses the alarm clock and submits to Rhineheart's 'flat, deferential compliance.'
Smith offers to wipe Neo's record clean in exchange for Morpheus; Neo refuses with contempt, and his mouth seals shut.

torn_between: Morpheus's framing of him as 'the One' and the destiny of the prophecy
His own disbelief and fear that he is not the chosen one
internal_conflicts.what_it_costs: He is beaten to the floor in the dojo, fails the rooftop jump and injures himself, and later dies in the hotel hallway — shot three times — before returning to life.

Her duty, discipline, and the crew's mission
internal_conflicts.what_it_costs: She must hold her grief silently while watching Neo die, then actively refuse the accepted ending — risking everything on a kiss — before she can release what she held.

The longing for the comfortable, verifiable illusion of the Matrix (the steak, the wine)

perspectives.label: THEY — the world-level collision
perspectives.stance_on_dilemma: The world frames the dilemma as a tactical calculation with a near-certain answer: when Morpheus is taken, the rational, survivable move is to cut the loss and escape. The Agents treat Morpheus as a broken key whose value is about to expire (ev-031: 'doubled serum dosage... the sign he is about to break'), and even the crew's own survival protocol is to pull Morpheus's plug rather than mount a rescue (ev-032: 'stops the plug from being pulled'). The objective situation prices self-preservation (

evidence.grounding: Smith escalates to a doubled serum dosage that drives Morpheus's alpha pattern into an ordered wave — the sign he is about to break — rendering him, in world-logic, a lost asset.
The crew's default is to pull Morpheus's plug and abandon him; Neo's act is to interrupt that accepted, survival-first procedure.

When the ship is hunted, Morpheus immediately converts to survival protocol — reading the Sentinels, giving the crew minutes, ordering the EMP charged — the world's instinct being to preserve the ship, not to gamble on one man.

perspectives.label: I — the protagonist's inside view
perspectives.stance_on_dilemma: Neo resolves the dilemma from the inside not by logic but by refusing the arithmetic of it. He explicitly denies he is the One (ev-032), so going back has no prophetic cover — it is a pure wager on a man. His choice is framed as the only thing he can live with after Morpheus already gave his life for him (ev-025), making self-preservation a cost to his emerging self-respect he will not pay.

evidence.grounding: Neo stops Morpheus's plug from being pulled and commits to the rescue while denying he is the One — 'a wager on a man rather than a prophecy... something he cannot justify logically, only believe in.'
Morpheus pins an Agent and orders Trinity to get Neo out, 'choosing to give his own life so the others can escape' — the debt of sacrifice Neo is answering.
When cornered in the subway, urged to run, Neo does not run — he 'turns back from the escalator to face the hunter,' the same refusal to flee carrying through to the end.

perspectives.label: YOU — whoever challenges the protagonist's worldview
perspectives.stance_on_dilemma: Morpheus is the living argument for the sacrifice horn — he has already enacted it (ev-025) and, even while being tortured, spends his last agency fighting to keep his mind from cracking rather than saving himself by breaking (ev-031). His faith reframes Neo's illogical gamble as destiny (ev-035: 'reinterprets both the prophecy and Trinity's silence as confirmation'), pressing Neo toward the belief that a man is worth any risk.

evidence.grounding: Morpheus models the sacrifice horn directly, giving his life so Neo and Trinity escape.
Captured and drugged, Morpheus 'spends his last agency fighting to keep his mind from cracking' — refusing self-preservation through betrayal of the crew.
After the rescue, Morpheus reinterprets the prophecy and Trinity's silence as confirmation of the One, converting Neo's faith-wager back into destiny and validating the sacrifice path.

perspectives.label: WE — a bond under the dilemma
perspectives.stance_on_dilemma: The Neo–Trinity bond is where the dilemma is felt as loyalty versus survival. Trinity, gutted by Morpheus's condition and Neo's self-denial, converts grief into command and makes the rescue possible only on her terms (ev-032), then refuses to accept Neo's death at all (ev-044). Their 'we' is the force that overrides the world's cut-the-loss logic — she will not let him be sacrificed, and will not let Morpheus be abandoned.

evidence.grounding: Trinity, 'gutted by both Morpheus's condition and Neo's self-denial, converts her grief into command and insists on' directing the rescue — binding herself to Neo's wager.
When the crew gives Neo up after he is shot, 'Trinity refuses the ending: she takes hold of his body and kisses him, and the monitors jump back to life' — the bond overriding the survival verdict.
Inside the exit, Neo 'breaks free of Trinity's embrace, and sends her out first' — the protective reciprocity of the bond even amid escape.

perspectives.label: WE (group) — a group living the question
perspectives.stance_on_dilemma: The crew collectively lives out both horns. Cypher embodies self-preservation to its logical end — recasting Morpheus's prophecy as a mere 'body count' (ev-020) and then trading Morpheus and the crew to save himself (ev-029). The rest of the crew — Tank, Switch, Apoc, Dozer — are the ones who pay the price of the sacrifice horn, and whose split between 'doubters and believers' (ev-016) shows a community wrestling with whether any one man is worth dying for.

evidence.grounding: Cypher 'recasts Morpheus's prophecy as a body count, telling him five before him took on an Agent and died,' embodying the self-preservation horn and retreating Neo toward caution.
Cypher completes the self-preservation horn by murdering Apoc and Switch and delivering Morpheus to the Agents to save himself — only struck down by the surviving Tank.
During Neo's failed jump, 'the crew watches the attempt split between doubters and believers' — the group's live argument over faith in one man versus prudent self-regard.
